reason: Crossing orbits may bring rocky planetesimals together, starting the growth of an embryo.
expectation: I expect collisions or accumulation to produce a larger rocky body, though some material may break apart.

alternatives.reason: Breaking the differentiated body could supply fragments, but I want to start growing an embryo first.

effect: The impacts produced several growing embryos, so I can now pursue their growth.
reaction: It is satisfying that crossing orbits led to accretion rather than only breakage.
reason: Gravitational focusing should help the embryos gather more material and advance toward a rocky world.
expectation: I expect a larger growing embryo, though I don't know which world it will become.

alternatives.reason: Adding rocky planetesimals also seems like a direct way to grow the embryos, but I want to see gravitational focusing in action.

effect: Gravitational focusing produced an embryo that can now gather rocky fragments more effectively.
reaction: The explanation makes the accelerating growth clear.
reason: Add rocky fragments to the strongly attracting embryo to continue building a world.
expectation: I expect the embryo to grow by incorporating the fragments, though its identity is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Adding planetesimals could grow another embryo, but I want to continue the current branch.

effect: The rocky fragments formed the proto-Earth; it still needs volatile-bearing material to meet the goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see which embryo becomes Earth.
reason: Break the differentiated small world to make more material available for growth.
expectation: I expect fragments from the body's interior, possibly including metal, though their next use is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: This could grow another embryo, but I want to pursue the material needed for proto-Earth first.

effect: The collision exposed metal-rich core fragments that can now be added to proto-Earth.
reaction: The connection to iron meteorites is interesting; the fragments are more than generic building material.
reason: Add the core fragments to proto-Earth to continue its growth.
expectation: I expect proto-Earth to incorporate metal, though it may still need water-bearing material afterward.

alternatives.reason: This could advance the other embryo, but I want to continue the proto-Earth branch.

effect: Proto-Earth has incorporated metal from an already differentiated body; adding water-bearing material can advance the volatile-bearing goal.
reaction: The inherited metal links small-body differentiation to Earth's continuing growth.
reason: Add water-bearing asteroid material to build a volatile-bearing young Earth.
expectation: I expect proto-Earth to acquire water-related hydrogen, though not necessarily liquid surface water.

alternatives.reason: Growing another embryo also serves a goal, but I want to finish the proto-Earth branch first.

effect: The young Earth now contains volatile-bearing material, completing that goal; another rocky embryo remains to be grown.
reaction: The uncertainty about water sources makes the outcome more nuanced.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the remaining embryo goal.
expectation: I expect the embryos to accrete rocky planetesimals and produce another growing rocky body.

effect: The remaining combination produced Theia and completed both chapter goals; its exact properties remain uncertain.
reaction: Theia's appearance makes me curious about the next encounter, while the uncertainty keeps the scenario grounded.

mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking the differentiated body to expose core fragments was most worthwhile: it connected a game action to iron meteorites and Earth's inherited material.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding rocky fragments to the attracting embryo felt fairly predictable, though it established which body would become Earth.

surprise.text: I was struck that iron meteorites can sample the exposed cores of differentiated parent bodies.

arbitrary.text: Adding core fragments to proto-Earth had a clear material purpose, but the particular pairing felt somewhat prescribed by the compatible-options menu.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the hypothetical encounter with Theia unfolds and what it explains about the Moon.
